questions.question: A telemetry table uses PRIMARY KEY ((tenant_id), event_time). One tenant produces most of the writes. What is the central risk?
options: Clustering by event_time automatically spreads the tenant across token owners
All of that tenant's writes still target one logical partition and its replica set
Increasing the replication factor splits the partition into independent shards
The coordinator permanently becomes the primary for that tenant
questions.explanation: The partition key, not the clustering column, determines the token and replica set. Replication makes copies of the same hot partition; it does not subdivide the key.

questions.question: Why is ((tenant_id, device_id, event_day), event_time, event_id) a useful key for a device telemetry read?
options: It supports arbitrary joins across every device
It distributes active devices, bounds the partition by day, and orders rows inside that partition
It guarantees every tenant-wide query touches one partition
It removes the need to estimate skew and retention
questions.explanation: The composite partition key matches a device-by-day lookup and spreads concurrent device writes. Clustering columns provide deterministic order inside that bounded partition.

questions.question: A keyspace has NetworkTopologyStrategy with RF=3 in us_east and RF=3 in eu_west. How many full replicas does one partition have across those datacenters?
questions.explanation: NetworkTopologyStrategy applies the replication factor independently in each datacenter. Three copies in each of two datacenters produce six full replicas.

questions.question: In a single-datacenter RF=3 replica set, one replica is unavailable. Which pair can both complete and has R + W > RF?
options: Write ONE and read ONE
Write QUORUM and read QUORUM
Write ALL and read ONE
Write ONE and read ALL
questions.explanation: With two replicas available, QUORUM writes and reads can each collect two responses. Their thresholds sum to four, which is greater than RF 3, so the successful acknowledgement sets must overlap.

questions.question: A QUORUM write times out. What may the client safely conclude?
options: No replica applied the mutation
Every replica applied the mutation
The coordinator did not collect enough acknowledgements before the timeout, so retry handling must tolerate a partial application
The partition key was not hashed
questions.explanation: A timeout is ambiguous. Some replicas may have applied the mutation even though the coordinator could not collect the required acknowledgements in time, so retries must be idempotent.

questions.question: Why must repair complete before tombstones are purged from replicas that may have missed a delete?
options: Repair converts every table to LeveledCompactionStrategy
A stale replica can later return an old live value after the deletion marker is gone
Tombstones are the only durable backup format
Compaction cannot read immutable SSTables
questions.explanation: A tombstone communicates a distributed delete. If it disappears before a stale replica learns the deletion, that replica's old value can become visible again.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates repair from compaction?
options: Compaction compares replicas across nodes; repair only merges files on one node
Both are names for the same SSTable rewrite
Repair synchronizes divergent replicas, while compaction merges SSTables and manages amplification on one node
Repair is a complete substitute for tested backups
questions.explanation: Repair compares replicas for shared token ranges and streams differences. Compaction rewrites local SSTables to reconcile versions and control read, write, and space amplification; neither replaces backup recovery.

questions.question: Why can TimeWindowCompactionStrategy fit TTL-based time-series data?
options: It turns every query into a cross-partition join
It groups data by time window so SSTables whose contents expire together can be removed efficiently
It eliminates write amplification and repair
It makes out-of-order timestamps irrelevant
questions.explanation: TWCS groups writes into time windows, which can align SSTable lifetime with TTL expiration. The workload must still test late writes, window sizing, repair, and I/O headroom.
